hypothesis: Moving coordinate-mapping disruption to episode1, before dual-sentinel detection can use a prior sensor trace, should increase unavoidable pre-detection mismatches. Corrective decoding may still mitigate post-detection mismatches but cannot repair earlier actions.
lineage: Frozen Y069/Y065 candidate and original public dual-sentinel/read-budget/matching evaluator. Exactly same arms/policies/physical legality, new development and sealed seeds.
primary: For each source pair report per-arm total/pre/post-detection mismatch episodes, detection counts, matching search, writes, physical legality and public scalar read budget. EARLY_CAUSAL_GAIN if steady zero, both pairs >=50% post-detection reduction vs dual detect-only and total corrected less than original rotating; PARTIAL_EARLY_GAIN if safety holds and at least one pair >=20% post-detection improvement; otherwise NO_GAIN. Do not treat residual pre-detection errors as recovered.
controls: Simulator physical labels exclusively evaluator-side, no future or post-hoc physical mapping passed to candidate
All arms ten public reads per trial, seven legal active assignments, maximum nine retained cache entries
Preregister one fresh sealed population distinct from Y069; no replay of previous Y069 original
Archive every trial incl adverse/null; one full pytest regression, no accepted ref/FORGE authority changes
claim_limit: Synthetic coordinate-disruption onset-timing study with bounded public sensors; no universal memory, production, or independently admitted scientific acceptance.
